To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rbcL pseudogene of Orobanche cernua and Orobanche ramosa have few indels in common, suggesting that their common ancestor had an intact rabcL reading frame.

1) The rbcL gene of Orobanche corymbosa is an intact open reading frame, whereas the rbcL genes of Orobanche ramosa and O. cernuam are pseudogenes, and 2) the rbcL pseudogene of O. fascicula contains a single nucleotide change that could restore the open reading frame.

rbcL pseudogene sequences are more likely to retain an open reading framework than predicted by a random model of substitution processes, and that the 3'-UTRs of rbcL in parasitic species of Nicotiana, Cuscutta and Orobanche have deletions compared to their photosynthetically competent relatives.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rbcL sequences from Orobanche are not pseudogenes by chance, but are either pseudogenes that have retained an open reading frame, or are functional genes that have retained a bias in synonymous substitutions.
the rbcL genes of O. corymboosa and O. corymosa have retained an open reading frame, whereas O. ramoso and O. cernuo have rbcL psedogenes.

the rbcL pseudogene in O. cernu and O. ramsosa is the result of a single event, whereas the rbcL sequences in O. cormbosa and O. fasculata are the result of multiple events, and the rbcL sequence in O. ramosis is the result of two independent events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rbcL is not a pseudogene in all nonphotosynthetic angiosperms, but rather that rbcL may be maintained as an intact reading frame in some nonphotosyntethic species.
the evolution of nonphotosynthetic parasitic plants has been complex, and the rbcL pseudogene may be a relic from an ancient ancestor of these plants.
the photosynthetic genes rbcL and rpoC2 are present as pseudogenes in some species and intact in others, whereas the rbcL 1st intron is absent from all Orobanche species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nonphotosynthetic parasitic plants have retained the rbcL pseudogene, and that the gene has retained an open reading frame in at least two species.
rbcL pseudogene sequences can provide useful information about the timing of the loss of photosynthesis in nonphotosynthetic parasitic plants.
rbcL is retained in nonphotosynthetic holoparasites, but it is a pseudogene in the majority of these species.
